pr_title: Bluetooth: ATT: Fix not restoring buffer state when send fails
pr_body:
Since bt_l2cap_send_cb can fail returning its error is not enough as
the buffer has been modified to add the headers, so this save the state
before calling bt_conn_send_cb and takes a reference so it can be
restored its original state in case of error.

Fixes #27434

Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
pr_comments: @joerchan @jhedberg any comments? I guess we want to process this one quickly given it fixes a high priority bug.
@mniestroj Can you please confirm that the updated PR fixes the reported issue?

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: L2CAP: buffer use after free
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Commit f4192bda26a1c7770e3d4c50235a6760f0506a0d ("Bluetooth: ATT: Add support EATT bearer") changed bt_att_sent() implementation, so packets that were not successfully sent are pushed back to queue:
```
		if (chan_send(chan, buf, NULL) < 0) {
			/* Push it back if it could not be send */
			k_queue_prepend(&att->tx_queue._queue, buf);
			break;
		}
```
There is however a problem in `chan_send` -> `bt_l2cap_send_cb` path, because buffer is being modified there (prepended with 4 header bytes in `bt_l2cap_send_cb()`) and freed (in `bt_conn_send_cb()`) when buffer is not sent successfully (e.g. no connection).

**To Reproduce**
Used `mcumgr` with `image list` command and a custom application + custom board. Target crashes when `mcumgr` disconnects because of timeout. Can provide more info if needed, but I think that bug is clear enough to notice looking at the code only.

**Expected behavior**
Getting rid of "use after free".

**Impact**
Undefined behavior (e.g. MPU FAULT crashes).

**Logs and console output**


review_comments: The resending logic it mentions is for the request itself, not for chan_send, the buffer is released at att_handle_rsp, we wouldn't keep a reference in bt_att_req if we expected it to be consumed. That said the error path seems wrong now, it would not free the buffer just the extra reference, what we should do is only take a reference if chan_send succeeds.

Actually we always do prepend it back to att->reqs in case of an error, so it looks like it was broken already as release the reference and reset the req->buf to NULL, weird that we didn't hit this before though.
Ive end up fixing the behavior of chan_req_send so it doesn't reset the req->buf to NULL.
